description:
What does it do?
Adding support for the strapi transfer command; running this command the user can chose the kind of operation to run and insert the needed data (url and token). Furthermore, the URL and token values fall back to dedicated environment variables value.
![425207109-2f6070c0-1053-4945-bd16-4f5baf4ef1f4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9bbe16d8-8532-4388-a2ac-2a6d2dd162c3)



Why is it needed?
Inserting the many and long options needed to transfer/push or transfer/pull data can be confusing and difficult; and it's so even more when the transfer is run iteratively.

How to test it?
Just run the strapi transfer command and enjoy the journey.
Set the STRAPI_TRANSFER_URL and STRAPI_TRANSFER_TOKEN env variables to enjoy it even more.

And eventually we need to make it retry with /admin if it doesn't have it and the initial connection fails
Can we keep the error check in its own hook?  basically leave the exact code that was already there, and just put it after your new hook?

```suggestion
            console.info(); // Empty line for better readability
```
Since we used .info above
Should we make it clear from the beginning that the /admin part of the path is expected? (currently it's only in the error handling)
So if a token is provided, it takes precedence over the env value?
@maccomaccomaccomacco what do you think? I think it's a good idea I just don't see how to reasonably fit it into one line.
Yeah, that's how I usually expect most tools to work. env values used by default, but provide a mechanism to override it case-by-case using the cli.
I don't think we can do much more than say "Enter the _admin_ URL of the remote Strapi instance to..."

For now let's leave it, but I think a future improvement could be that if we do not detect it ends with '/admin' we log a warning message. That would basically solve the problem and we wouldn't need the more complex solutions we've discussed before (like appending it and retrying connection)
It's not always /admin as that can be changed so we need to accommodate for that if we do
Can't we just let the user put the base Url and get the admin path from the admin configuration?
